chunks: Those to whom We have given the Book know it distinctly as they know their sons; but those who are lost of soul do not believe.

key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: The Book (referring to the Torah and/or Gospel)
key_terms.خَسِرُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ: They lost their souls (through disbelief or negligence)

ai.seo_question: Why do the People of the Book reject the truth despite knowing it clearly?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the paradox of 'knowledge without faith' (ilm bi-la amal), where the People of the Book possess clear, intuitive recognition of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the Torah and Gospel, yet their stubborn arrogance (istikbar) prevents acceptance. This reflects the concept that mere intellectual acknowledgment is insufficient for salvation if not accompanied by the humility of the heart, a theme central to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings on the prerequisites of true belief.
